newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea steps in to cap won's fall vs dlr.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea steps in to cap won's fall vs dlr.

text.p: The central Bank of Korea intervened repeatedly in the interbank market in early afternoon trading on Thursday to support the falling won against the dollar, dealers said.
But the bank denied the action, as it routinely does.
The Bank of Korea came in when the won hit the new six-year low of 847.10 in the afternoon. Traders said the bank had also sold dollars earlier in the day.
Large import deals have sparked brisk dollar buying, putting pressure on the local unit throughout the day, traders said.
Traders said the won was expected to decline further without the central bank's support, traders said.
The won was trading at 846.60 during afternoon trading.
